merger_description:
L'Oréal S.A. and its subsidiaries (**L'Oréal**), through its wholly-owned subsidiary L'Oréal India Private Limited, proposes to acquire 65.22% of the share capital of Onesto Labs Private Limited (**Innovist**).

L'Oréal conducts research, development, manufacturing, marketing, distribution and sale of beauty and personal care products. In Australia, L'Oréal sells haircare, skincare, makeup and fragrances wholesale through pharmacies, supermarkets and retailers, as well as through their own branded retail stores YSL Beauty Boutiques, Aesop and Kiehl’s.

L'Oréal supplies key brands in Australia such as L'Oréal, Garnier, Maybelline, Lancôme, Yves Saint Laurent, Vichy, La Roche Posay, Kérastase, Aesop and Kiehl’s.

Innovist manufactures and sells beauty and personal care products. Innovist sells hair care, skincare and sun care products under the brand names Bare Anatomy, Chemist at Play, SunScoop and Vinci. In Australia, Innovist sells its Bare Anatomy and Chemist at Play products directly to consumers.

determination_table_content.details:
L'Oréal S.A. and its subsidiaries (L'Oréal), through its wholly-owned
subsidiary L'Oréal India Private Limited, proposed acquisition of
65.22% of the share capital of Onesto Labs Private Limited (Innovist)
(the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, L'Oréal, conducts research, development,
manufacturing, marketing, distribution and sale of beauty and
personal care products. In Australia, L'Oréal sells haircare, skincare,
makeup and fragrances through pharmacies, supermarkets and
retailers, as well as through their own branded retail stores YSL
Beauty Boutiques, Aesop and Kiehl’s.
The target, Innovist, manufactures and sells beauty and personal
care products. Innovist sells hair care, skincare and sun care
products under the brand names Bare Anatomy, Chemist at Play,
SunScoop and Vinci. In Australia, Innovist sells its Bare Anatomy and
Chemist at Play products directly to consumers via online platforms.

L'Oréal and Innovist (together, the Parties) overlap in the supply of
beauty and personal care products. L'Oréal supplies beauty and
personal care products at both the wholesale and retail level.
Innovist supplies beauty and personal care products, specifically hair
and skin care products, body wash, and deodorant.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings
• The increase in L'Oréal’s market share in the supply of
beauty and personal care products in Australia as a result of
the Acquisition is low, given Innovist’s low sales in Australia.
• L’Oréal would continue to face competition from alternative
retail suppliers of beauty and personal care products in
Australia post-acquisition.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
